subject.title: config: use datetime suffix for config backup files instead of numeric rotation

question: Should OpenClaw core replace the shipped numbered config backup ring with timestamped backup names, and what legacy-backup migration policy is required?
rationale: This changes a shipped recovery and sensitive-file handling contract, so automation should not choose whether existing `.bak.N` recovery points may be deleted, preserved, or converted.

options.title: Require Migration-Safe Timestamp Backups
options.body: Sponsor the timestamp naming change only after the PR preserves or converts existing numbered backups, handles timestamp collisions, hardens all retained backups, and proves fresh-install plus upgrade behavior.

options.title: Keep The Numeric Ring
options.body: Reject the timestamp suffix change for now and treat the numbered `.bak.1` through `.bak.4` ring as the stable recovery contract.

options.title: Accept First-Run Cleanup
options.body: Intentionally allow the new datetime cleanup to prune existing numbered backups on upgrade, accepting the recovery-point loss as product policy.

recommendation.title: Require Migration-Safe Timestamp Backups
recommendation.body: Sponsor the timestamp naming change only after the PR preserves or converts existing numbered backups, handles timestamp collisions, hardens all retained backups, and proves fresh-install plus upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest visible history on the backup rotation helper and config recovery semantics.
